facts.value: An electric circuit is an interconnection of electric components such that electric charge is made to flow along a closed path (a circuit), usually to perform some useful task.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: The components in an electric circuit can take many forms, which can include elements such as resistors, capacitors, switches, transformers, and electronics.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: Electronic circuits contain active components, usually semiconductors, and typically exhibit non-linear behaviour, requiring complex analysis.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: The simplest electric components are those that are termed passive and linear: while they may temporarily store energy, they contain no sources of it, and exhibit linear responses to stimuli.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: The resistor is perhaps the simplest of passive circuit elements, as its name suggests, it resists the current through it, dissipating its energy as heat.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: Ohm's law is a basic law of circuit theory, stating that the current passing through a resistance is directly proportional to the potential difference across it.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: The ohm, the unit of resistance, was named in honour of Georg Ohm, and is symbolised by the Greek letter Ω.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: The capacitor is a device that can store charge, and thereby storing electrical energy in the resulting field.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: The unit of capacitance is the farad, named after Michael Faraday, and given the symbol F.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: One farad is the capacitance that develops a potential difference of one volt when it stores a charge of one coulomb.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: The inductor is a conductor, usually a coil of wire, that stores energy in a magnetic field in response to the current through it.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: The induced voltage is proportional to the time rate of change of the current.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: The unit of inductance is the henry, named after Joseph Henry.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering

facts.value: One henry is the inductance that will induce a potential difference of one volt if the current through it changes at a rate of one ampere per second.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering
